newsitem.title: USA: Much of central U.S. shivers in arctic cold.
newsitem.headline: Much of central U.S. shivers in arctic cold.

text.p: An arctic cold wave that sent shivers through residents from Canada to Mexico eased its grip on Friday, although forecasters warned that even chillier weather may arrive in time for Christmas.
The frigid weather slowed the pace of Christmas shopping in the U.S. Midwest, and had tourists in New Orleans' French Quarter muttering about not bringing enough warm clothing.
This week's cold front also kicked energy prices sharply higher, nearly doubling wholesale electricity prices in the eastern half of the nation.
"We're past the peak of this cold air mass. From here until Sunday it will be warming up," said Joel Burgio, a forecaster with Weather Services Corp.
The warmer forecast was welcome ahead of the one of the busiest travel weekends of the year as people planned to set off on Christmas vacations.
But a storm early next week was expected to drop either rain or snow on a swath of the Midwest, followed by another, even colder, arctic blast in time for Christmas, Burgio said.
South Dakota has already received half its usual winter allotment of 26 inches (66 cm) of snow, and winter does not officially begin until Saturday.
The coldest temperature was 18 degrees below zero (minus 28 Celsius) in Minneapolis, with Chicago recording 4 degrees (minus 15 degrees Celsius) and Des Moines, Iowa, 6 below (minus 21 Celsius).
Schools across the region gradually reopened, and crews dodged abandoned cars as they cleared icy snowdrifts from several highways shut down since the blizzard.

In New Orleans, where residents awoke to a second day of sub-freezing temperatures, city officials opened up public and university buildings as shelters. Watering troughs serving the French Quarter's horse-drawn carriage trade froze.
The cold also hampered divers inspecting the Riverwalk shopping area along the Mississippi River for damage from last Saturday's accident with a disabled freighter.

The Gulf Coast remained chilly after witnessing a rare snowfall earlier in the week. The low temperature in Tallahassee, Florida, was 24 degrees (minus 4 Celsius), and Orlando residents felt a chill at 34 degrees (1 Celsius).
